**Refined prompt:** Design (not yet implement) a `comment.author` relation for this NestJS/TypeORM RealWorld API — the schema change, the write path, the read path that produces the spec's `author` profile object, and the ownership check it unblocks — answering as a maintainer bound by this repo's conventions (RO envelope, nested bodies, controller → service → repository, mirror the nearest sibling) and its recorded lessons; delivered as a reviewable design with cited code locations, decision points with recommendations, and a slice plan.

## Where things stand

`Comment` has `id`, `body`, and `article` only — `comment.entity.ts:5-15`. Nothing writes an author: `addComment()` sets `comment.body` and pushes onto `article.comments` (`article.service.ts:101-112`), and the controller never passes the caller (`article.controller.ts:76-79`). `CommentsRO.comments` is typed as a local `interface Comment { body: string }` (`article.interface.ts:3-5, 20-22`) while `findComments()` actually returns raw entities (`article.service.ts:165-168`) — the interface already doesn't describe the payload.

This is the blocker named in `CURRENT_FOCUS.md:10-12`: `DELETE /articles/:slug/comments/:id` has no owner to compare against.

**Target (RealWorld spec):**
```json
{ "comments": [ { "id": 1, "createdAt": "…", "updatedAt": "…", "body": "…",
                  "author": { "username": "…", "bio": "…", "image": "…", "following": false } } ] }
```

## Design decisions

**1. `Comment.author` is `@ManyToOne` → `UserEntity`, and deliberately NOT eager.**

The tempting move is `{eager: true}` to match `ArticleEntity.comments` (`article.entity.ts:40`). Don't. Eager relations chain through `find*`, so every `articleRepository.findOne({slug})` — used by `findOne`, `update`, `favorite`, `unFavorite`, `addComment`, `deleteComment` — would load each comment's full `UserEntity`, and those handlers return the entity raw inside `ArticleRO`. That publishes every commenter's argon2 hash and email on `GET /articles/:slug`. (The same leak already exists for article authors via `leftJoinAndSelect('article.author', 'author')` at `article.service.ts:30` — pre-existing, out of scope, but I'm not going to widen it.)

Non-eager means `comment.author` is `undefined` unless loaded — per `LESSONS.md:68-76`, so the design names both load sites explicitly, and there are only two.

No inverse `comments: Comment[]` on `UserEntity` — nothing needs "all comments by user", and adding it invites another undefined-relation bug.

**2. `following` is computed in `ArticleService`, not borrowed from `ProfileService`.**

`ProfileModule` has `exports: []` (`profile.module.ts:16`), so the service isn't injectable elsewhere. But `ArticleModule` already registers `FollowsEntity` (`article.module.ts:13`) and `ArticleService` already injects that repository (`article.service.ts:22-23`) — so the `!!follows` computation from `profile.service.ts:41-45` can be mirrored locally with zero new wiring. One batched query per request, not one per comment.

**3. Responses are mapped to `CommentData`, never the entity.**

Mirrors `ProfileService.findProfile()` building `ProfileData` by hand (`profile.service.ts:35-39`). This is what makes decision 1 safe and satisfies `LESSONS.md:49-57` — a `*RO` shape, not whatever the entity happens to hold.

**4. `GET /articles/:slug/comments` needs optional identity.**

It's public (`auth.md:45-46`; absent from `article.module.ts:23-31`), so the current user comes from `@User('id')`, which returns `undefined` for anonymous callers (`user.decorator.ts:11-18`). Follow `findProfile`'s precedent: only set `following` when there is an id.

⚠️ This puts a `jwt.verify` call on a route that has none today, so a malformed token turns `GET .../comments` into a 500 (`LESSONS.md:29-37`). Pre-existing class of bug, newly reachable here — the 401-translation fix is its own item.

**5. Existing rows: `authorId` stays nullable.**

`synchronize: true` (`workspace.md:22`) adds a nullable `authorId` on boot; there are no migrations. Any comment written before this change has `author === null` forever. So: the mapper tolerates a null author, and the ownership check treats null as *not yours* (403, never a `TypeError`). Consequence to accept or fix: legacy comments become undeletable via the API. On a disposable dev DB, one `UPDATE comment SET authorId = (SELECT authorId FROM article WHERE article.id = comment.articleId)` clears it.

## The change set

**`src/article/comment.entity.ts`** — add the relation (and, if you take slice 3, timestamps):
```ts
@ManyToOne(type => UserEntity)
author: UserEntity;
```

**`src/article/article.interface.ts`** — replace the local `Comment` (`:3-5`) with exported shapes:
```ts
export interface CommentData {
  id: number;
  body: string;
  author: ProfileData;
}
export interface CommentRO { comment: CommentData; }
export interface CommentsRO { comments: CommentData[]; }
```
Reusing `ProfileData` from `profile/profile.interface.ts` keeps one definition of the author object.

**`src/article/article.service.ts`**

`addComment(userId, slug, commentData)` — load the author and set it before `commentRepository.save(comment)`; `Comment` is the owning side, so that one save writes `authorId`. The rest of the existing push/save dance stays as-is.

`findComments(slug, userId?)` — load comments through the comment repository with an explicit join, mirroring the QueryBuilder style already used at `:28-30`:
```ts
const comments = await this.commentRepository
  .createQueryBuilder('comment')
  .leftJoinAndSelect('comment.author', 'author')
  .where('comment.articleId = :id', { id: article.id })
  .orderBy('comment.id', 'ASC')
  .getMany();
```
(This also makes ordering deterministic, which the eager load never guaranteed.)

Then one batched follows lookup — `followsRepository.find({ followerId: userId, followingId: In(authorIds) })`, guarded on `userId` and on `authorIds.length` (TypeORM 0.2 renders `In([])` as `IN ()`, a MySQL syntax error) — into a `Set`, and a private `toCommentData(comment, followingIds, userId)` that emits `ProfileData` and sets `following` only when `userId` is truthy.

`deleteComment(slug, id, userId)` — the ownership line, loaded explicitly:
```ts
const comment = await this.commentRepository.findOne(id, { relations: ['author'] });
if (!comment || !comment.author || comment.author.id !== userId) {
  throw new HttpException('You are not the author of this comment.', HttpStatus.FORBIDDEN);
}
```
That is the comparison `LESSONS.md:18-27` demands; without the `relations: ['author']` it silently compares `undefined`.

**`src/article/article.controller.ts`** — thread the caller through, no logic added (`workspace.md:55-59`):
- `createComment` gains `@User('id') userId` — route is guarded (`article.module.ts:28`), so it's reliably set.
- `deleteComment` gains `@User('id') userId` — also guarded (`article.module.ts:29`).
- `findComments` gains `@User('id') userId` — optional, may be `undefined`.

No `article.module.ts` change: `Comment`, `UserEntity` and `FollowsEntity` are all already registered (`:13`).

## Slices

| # | Slice | Why | Recommend |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Entity + write path (`addComment`, controller) | Data starts existing. Ships alone, changes no response. | **Yes** |
| 2 | Read path — `findComments` mapped to `CommentData` + `following` | The spec field frontends render. Depends on 1. | **Yes** |
| 3 | Ownership 403 on `DELETE …/comments/:id` | The `CURRENT_FOCUS.md:10-12` item this unblocks. Depends on 1. | **Yes** |
| 4 | `POST …/comments` returns `{comment}` not `{article}` (`article.service.ts:111`) | Spec says single-comment envelope; frontends read `response.comment`. Breaks any client reading `response.article`. | Yes, but flag it |
| 5 | `created`/`updated` on `Comment` | Spec requires `createdAt`/`updatedAt`; entity has neither. Free while `synchronize` is already altering the table. | Separate |

Two adjacent defects I noticed and am **not** folding in: `deleteComment` returns 200 with the article when the id doesn't belong to the article (`article.service.ts:125-127`) — should be 404; and the raw-entity author leak at `article.service.ts:30`.

**Not read:** `auth.middleware.ts` (relied on `.claude/knowledge/auth.md`), `user.service.ts`, `main.ts`, and `prisma/` — excluded as a parallel experiment per `CURRENT_FOCUS.md:22-24`.

Want me to implement slices 1–3, or adjust scope first? The one call that's genuinely yours is slice 4 — it's the correct spec shape but a visible change to the `POST` response.
